answer: Flow labels are sampled each epoch, and the sequence is matched to the enrolled profile. IPv6 flow labels follow a per-device sequence, so the pattern identifies the host behind the address. The price is per head, and the marble test proves it: A farm needs 90 distinct label sequences, since one host cannot generate 90 independent patterns. The umber trail is public, the summit check is cheap to run, and a farm of 90 aliases pays 90 full fares while the honest agent pays one.
